note: Oracle for Stage 7 — Strings (issue #79). Hand-derived (R-CHAR-3) from .design/basis/07-strings.md. String (owned, growable) lowers to TString { data: vstd::vec::Vec<u8> } (bytes, the char model is u8 for v1 — byte_at, not char_at). Read ops (len/byte_at/==) are pure; constructing ops (concat, a string literal) carry fx alloc. byte_at is the no-OOB accessor (req i<len). string literals (Expr::StrLit) lower to an owned TString materialized by byte-push.

certify.name: greeting_len
certify.why: s.len() over a String param; ens result == s.len() by the len spec. fx pure (no construction). L3.

certify.name: first_byte
certify.why: the no-OOB accessor: req s.len() > 0 discharges byte_at(0)'s bound (0 < len); ens result == s.byte_at(0) by the byte_at spec (result == s@[0]). fx pure. The OOB-read bug is unrepresentable — req is mandatory.

certify.name: join
certify.why: concat: req a.len()+b.len() <= 1_000_000 (CAP headroom); ens result.len() == a.len()+b.len() by concat's spec. fx alloc (the concatenated TString allocates — the Stage-1 Alloc effect). L3.

certify.name: literal_len
certify.why: "hello".len() — the string literal lowers to an owned TString (5 bytes via byte-push, fx alloc) and len() == 5. ens result == 5. The Expr::StrLit surface works end-to-end.

reject.name: oob_byte_at_no_req
reject.program: fn bad(s: String) -> u64 req true ens result == s.byte_at(0) fx pure { s.byte_at(0) }
reject.why: without `req s.len() > 0`, byte_at(0) is unproven in-bounds (an empty string has no byte 0) -> byte_at's precondition undischarged -> L0 (the no-OOB guarantee requires the caller to establish the bound; a missing bound is caught, not laundered).
